p.i: Temporaque incedant velati frondis honore / Vatibus Italiae sueto nos propter amoenum / Eridanum Phaëtontea repetamus in umbra / Sparsa per astriferos late miracula campos, / Qua Pelusiaci cura est progressa magistri / Contentus nouisse polos, dum classica cessant, / Nec ferus Aonis Mars inuidet otia Musis.
Octo igitur solos veterum solertia coelos / Nouerat: & varij quot erant discrimina motus, / Æthera coelestes totidem diuisit in orbes.
Nec tamen (haec ratio quamuis monstrarit aperte) / Cessat adhuc caecis infcitia mersa tenebris, / Oblatrare palam, coelum damnare quiete, / Aufa pigram celeri motu conuertere terram.

Cum quibus indulsit sensum natura videndi, / Quotidie cernant noctis cedentibus umbris, / Mane novo Phoebum paulatim asurgere ponto, / Aut velut enasci longinquo ex aequore terra, / Inde per aduersum coeli confcendere cluuum, / Donec propositi victor stetit arduus alto / Culmine, & in cunctas radiorum spicula terras / Direxit, mox aequoreas decliuis in vndas / Precipitat celerem parvo moderamine currum, / Donec equos fessos Atlantide ferus in vnda / Abluat, & furtua cedat sua tempora noctis. / Sic vaga rorifera confurgit Delia biga, / Sic medij sensim potitur fastigia coeli. / Sic cadit in fluctus. Hac sidera lege ferena / Nocte per aetherios volunt sua lumina campos, / Primum humili, celsa mox lampade, rursus ad imum / Vsq; solum pressa, mox vt tellure vel vnda / Absorptum quaerunt spectantia lumina lumen.

page.notes: Verse printed in italic; lines run as one stanza with line ends marked by slashes. Some letters are worn (for example the initial of "Vatibus" and "Aonis"); readings there are the likeliest ones. The word "Deinde" is treated as a catchword.
